RHEUMATOLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-09-25
55M, general wellness examination with rheumatology review.

S:
Patient presents for a wellness visit with attention to his joint symptoms. He reports morning stiffness in both hands lasting more than an hour, with swelling and tenderness that makes gripping difficult. The past month has been worse despite his regimen. He works as a facilities technician and finds hand-intensive tasks hard. He could not complete 8 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. Mother with breast cancer. Appetite is fair; diet is high in sugary drinks, which was discussed. Sleep is interrupted by hand discomfort. Lives with his wife. Never smoker.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 74, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 182 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
Hands: symmetric swelling and tenderness at the MCP and PIP joints bilaterally, reduced grip strength.
Wrists: mild warmth, limited flexion.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Labs (this week): ESR 38 mm/hr, CRP elevated, Hgb 11.7 g/dL, A1c 6.1%, anti-CCP positive on prior testing.

A/P:
1. Rheumatoid arthritis with active synovitis of both hands. Continue methotrexate weekly with folic acid; discussed escalating therapy and ordered monitoring labs. Reviewed joint protection and referred to occupational therapy for hand splinting.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Discussed swapping sugary drinks for water and adding daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Family history: discussed mother's history and reviewed age-appropriate screening for the patient.
5. Function and work: hand limitations are affecting his usual shifts. Provided a letter outlining activity restrictions for his employer.

Return to clinic in 6 weeks to reassess joint activity and review labs, sooner if swelling worsens.
